agent_notes: The output can be large: a repository of 180 files gave 4 MB of JSON with the dictionary. Give --limit, --fields, or --summary first.
Findings alone never change the exit code. Ask for a gate when you want one.
A rule identifier is stable. Read it from this document, and not from the text of a message.
The dictionary is off by default, because it reports about 1 word in 10 of general software documentation.
ste review only prints an instruction: start a subagent with the ste-review skill. It reads no file and sends nothing.

--clear-cache.note: remove the disk cache of the grammar. $STE_GRAMMAR_CACHE gives the path of the cache, and the value off stops the cache.

baseline.note: the baseline command takes each flag of lint, and --dry-run. The dry run gives the plan: the path, the findings, the files, and the accepted findings that the new file keeps and removes.

--analyze.note: exit 2 when a fixture needs the analyzer and it cannot start. Without the flag, the run skips such a fixture and names it in skipped.

--fail-under.note: exit 1 when the precision or the recall is less

--force.note: write the file also when a config exists

commands.analyzer: Show the analyzer of the grammar and what it needs.
commands.baseline: Accept the findings of today, and report only the new ones after that.
commands.dict: Make a local index of the ASD-STE100 dictionary from your own copy.
commands.eval: Measure the rules against a labeled corpus.
commands.init: Write a start config, .ste.yml, in the current directory. It takes --dry-run, --force, and --format.
commands.lint: Check files, directories, or standard input.
commands.review: Print an instruction for an agent: run ste lint, then start a subagent that loads the ste-review skill for the rules that need a reader. It reads no file, sends nothing, and exits with 0.

analyzer.note: start the analyzer of the grammar for each run

max_noun_words.note: no default. Rule STE-1.9 reports nothing until this key gives a limit. The explanation of rule 1.9 gives 3 words.

prefer.note: the key is the name to use, and the list holds the other names of the same item. Rule STE-1.11 reads it.

description: A deterministic ASD-STE100 checker for Markdown and plain text.

exit_codes.0: The tool ran. Findings alone do not change this code.
exit_codes.2: A flag, a file, or the config has an error.

--all.note: read every file, including the files that git ignores

--analyze.note: use the analyzer of the grammar. Rules 2.1 and 5.3 need it, and it makes rules 3.5 and 3.6 more exact. Run "ste analyzer" to see what it needs.

--dry-run.note: for the baseline command: show the plan and write nothing

--fail-on-new.note: exit 1 when a finding is not in the baseline

--fail-over.note: exit 1 when the score for each 100 words is higher

--max-words.note: replaces the limit of the standard

--preset.note: add the technical nouns of a subject field

--use-dict.note: use the imported dictionary for STE-1.1

--warnings-as-errors.note: exit 1 when a warning exists; info stays advice

output.note: json gives one object with a flat findings list. ndjson gives one object for each line, each with a type of finding or summary. sarif gives SARIF 2.1.0 for code scanning. github gives one workflow command of GitHub Actions for each finding. sarif and github give each path from the top of the git work tree, and they do not use --fields.

paths: The project directory is the first directory, from the current directory upward, that holds a config file. The search stops at the top of the git work tree. A path in the config, each exclude pattern, and the default baseline start from the project directory. A key of the baseline is the path from the directory of the baseline file.

rules.name: Unapproved word or word group
rules.note: 0.95 and 0.6 come from the dictionary. 0.6 means that the dictionary has the word only as a verb, and the analyzer did not tag the word. With the analyzer, a verb gets 0.95, and a noun or an adjective gives no finding.

rules.name: British spelling
rules.note: A capitalized word that does not start a sentence is a name, thus the rule does not report it. With the analyzer, the rule also reports a pair that changes with the part of speech, such as "licence" and "practise". A word in quotation marks is a mention, and the analyzer part does not report it.

rules.name: Complex verb construction
rules.note: 0.9 for a perfect, or for "is to be" and a participle that the analyzer gives as a participle. 0.85 for "is to be" and a participle without the analyzer. 0.55 for "has been" and a word that is not a participle.

rules.name: Progressive -ing form
Passive voice
rules.note: 0.95 with a by-agent, 0.85 for an irregular participle, 0.7 for a participle that ends with ed.

rules.name: A noun for an action
rules.note: 0.9 for a word group of the list. 0.85 with the analyzer: a verb with little meaning, such as "perform" or "make", and its object, a noun that names an action.

rules.name: Contraction or omitted article
rules.note: 0.98 is a contraction, with the warning severity. 0.5 is a singular noun with no article, as a subject or an object, with the info severity. That part needs the analyzer, and only strict mode or a lower min_confidence shows it.

rules.name: Sentence too long
rules.note: 20 words for a numbered step, and 25 for other text. The text in parentheses is also a sentence with the same limit (rule 8.5). With the analyzer, a name of many words counts as one word (rule 8.6).

rules.name: Semicolon
Phrasal verb
rules.note: 0.85 for a phrasal verb of the list. With the analyzer, the rule also finds a particle with words between it and its verb. A phrasal verb that is not in the list gets 0.7.

rules.name: Latin abbreviation
rules.note: A general recommendation is advice and not a rule, thus no mode and no flag makes it an error.

rules.name: A list with two constructions
rules.note: The rule reports a list that starts some items with a capital letter and other items with a small letter.

rules.name: An instruction in a note
rules.note: The rule reads 5 words, such as "must". With the analyzer, it also reports a note that starts with a command, at 0.75. A reference such as "see" or "refer to" gives no finding.

rules.name: Paragraph too long
rules.note: 6 sentences maximum.

rules.name: A safety instruction with no explanation
rules.note: The rule reads a warning, a caution, and a danger block.

rules.name: A safety instruction with no word for the level of the risk
rules.note: The rule reads a note, a tip, an info, an attention, and an important block. It reports one that tells of an injury, of damage, or of a loss of data. It also reports a caution block that tells of an injury or of death, because that risk needs a warning.

rules.name: A condition after the command
rules.note: The rule reads a numbered step only. A condition that follows an infinitive belongs to the infinitive, and the rule does not report it. With the analyzer, it also reports a clause with "before", "after", or "once", and the words "in case" and "as soon as", after the command, at 0.75.

rules.name: Two names for the same item
rules.note: The rule reports nothing until the prefer key of the config gives the names. No tool can know that two nouns mean the same item.

rules.name: A technical noun that is too long
rules.note: The rule reads only the technical nouns of the config: allow.nouns and the names of prefer. It reports nothing until max_noun_words gives a limit. It reports the first use of each noun in a file.

rules.name: An instruction that is not a command
rules.note: The rule needs the analyzer. It reads a numbered step, and it steps over a condition clause.

rules.name: A noun of more than three words
rules.note: The rule needs the analyzer. A name of many words is one unit by rule 8.6, thus the rule does not report it.

rules.name: A verb form that is not an approved tense
rules.note: Reports would, should, shall, may, and might with a verb. 0.9 when the analyzer gives the modal and its verb, 0.8 from the words alone. A perfect after the modal goes to STE-3.4.

rules.name: A past participle that is not an adjective
rules.note: The rule needs the analyzer. It reports a participle that is the verb of a reduced clause. 0.8 with a by-agent, 0.7 without one. The severity is info, because it is not certain that rule 3.3 forbids a reduced clause, such as 'the file created by the tool'.

rules.name: A technical noun as a verb
rules.note: The rule needs the analyzer. It reads the one-word nouns of allow.nouns that are not also in allow.verbs. The nouns of the software preset are not technical nouns for this rule.

rules.name: A technical verb as a noun
rules.note: The rule needs the analyzer. It reads the one-word verbs of allow.verbs that are not also in allow.nouns. The rule does not report a verb before a noun, as in "the lint command".

rules.name: More than one instruction in a step
rules.note: The rule needs the analyzer. It reads a numbered step that starts with a command, and it reports a second command that joins the first. Actions at the same time, alternatives with "or", and two verbs with one object, such as "push and hold", give no finding.

rules.name: A safety instruction that does not start with a command
rules.note: The rule needs the analyzer. It reads the first sentence of a warning, a caution, and a danger block. It reports a sentence with a subject and a verb that is not a command. A phrase with no verb gives no finding.

rules.name: A word that is not the approved part of speech
rules.note: The rule needs --use-dict and the analyzer. It reports a verb that the dictionary approves only as a noun or an adjective, and a noun that it approves only as a verb. It does not read a heading or a table cell. The severity is info, because the precision was measured only with an invented dictionary.

rules.name: An adjective form that the dictionary does not give
rules.note: The rule needs --use-dict, the analyzer, and an index that has the forms. It reads a comparative or a superlative adjective.

rules.name: A verb form that the dictionary does not give
rules.note: The rule needs --use-dict, the analyzer, and an index that has the forms. It also applies rule 1.4 to a verb. STE-3.5 reports an -ing form.

rules.name: A compound modifier with no hyphen
rules.note: The rule needs the analyzer. It reports two words before a noun that modify it as one unit, such as "high pressure valve".

suppression.note: A directive with no rule identifier applies to every rule.
